subject.title: fix: discord exec approvals fails against local self-signed TLS gateway

question: Should maintainers adopt and rebase the open shared-bootstrap TLS fingerprint PR, or ask for a fresh replacement fix for this issue?
rationale: Current main still has the bug, but an open proof-positive PR already owns the right shared path and is conflicting, so opening another automated fix PR would duplicate active work and cross a TLS trust boundary.

options.title: Adopt and rebase the shared-bootstrap PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the canonical fix path, resolve conflicts, preserve the shared TLS semantics, and rerun focused gateway/bootstrap approval validation before merge.

options.title: Request a fresh replacement PR
options.body: Close or supersede the conflicting branch only if a new narrow PR preserves the shared resolver scope and proof coverage.

options.title: Defer without a new fix PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and avoid duplicate automation while accepting that local TLS approval/bootstrap clients remain broken.

recommendation.title: Adopt and rebase the shared-bootstrap PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80204 as the canonical fix path, resolve conflicts, preserve the shared TLS semantics, and rerun focused gateway/bootstrap approval validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared gateway auth/approval helper and TLS fingerprint history point to steipete as the clearest owner for choosing the canonical repair path.
